svg.text: Concurrent clocks — five orthogonal regions, all live at once
Harel convention: dashed lines separate orthogonal (concurrent) regions of one superstate. No region can be understood alone; the couplings at the bottom are the only channels between them.
REGION 1 — CROSS-BOOK FADE CLOCK · FadePhase, InterlinearNavProvider
after RECENTER_FADE_MS (500 ms) the reveal completes
held down through load + first-mount settle
an external nav arriving mid-reveal re-engages the curtain rather than fading fresh content twice
cancelFade() returns to idle from either non-idle state on a book load error, so the error is shown rather than hidden behind a curtain that will never receive a settle. [X6]
The fade-out is instant (transitionDuration 0ms), not a transition: the old book is swapped for the Loading placeholder in the very commit the curtain drops.
quiet 100 ms, or the 500 ms deadline backstop → onSettled [X1]
A boundary edit takes NO transition here. It shifts range by anchorDelta in place and syncs the display refs — an idle-to-idle self transition, because the user is looking at the edit. [X5]
Extends and culls are idle-to-idle too: range mutates with no fade, and scroll is corrected against a recorded anchor element before the browser paints.
scrollend, or the 600 ms fallback → commit, plus a re-center if the window moved mid-glide [X4]
after 500 ms: swap the display ref, snap, commit the active segment, holdCentered
A view-option toggle (simplifyPhrases, showMorphology) is a self transition on settled: instant centerGroup, no fade and no hold. hideInactiveLinkButtons is excluded — hidden slots keep their space.
Note the two meanings of “internal”: this region classifies by whether the STRIP emitted the change, region 2 by the nav marker. A segment-list click is internal there and external here. [X2]
REGION 4 — holdCentered · one at a time, a new hold supersedes the old
ResizeObserver fires — the dominant reflow lands 300-500 ms after mount, long after the quiet window lapsed
cancelled: the 2000 ms hard cap, a superseding hold, or a focus move [X3]
The observer’s lifetime is deliberately longer than the tick loop’s. Tearing it down when the loop goes idle would miss the late reflow and leave the focus stranded off centre —
which is precisely the intermittent “not centred on first load” failure this region exists to prevent.
REGION 5 — INTERNAL-NAV MARKER · one instance per verse key, held in a Map
consumeInternalNav matches → returns true, marker cleared
evicted at the start of the next consumeInternalNav
Why a TTL exists at all: React can batch two rapid clicks, and the host then echoes only the last of them — stranding the first marker with no echo ever coming. [X5]
Without expiry, a much later EXTERNAL navigation to that same verse would consume the stale marker and silently skip its recenter fade.
Cross-region couplings — the only channels between the regions

g.text: [X1] R2 → R1 reportSettled() at the end of the settle is the only thing that lifts the cross-book curtain. Over-calling is safe: the clock ignores it
unless a cross-book fade is actually awaiting settle, so a same-book recenter cannot lift a curtain that was never down.
[X2] R2 → R3 At the recenter midpoint the window flips displayContinuousScroll through a callback inside its own state batch, so the strip mounts
or unmounts in the same React commit as the window rebuild. Reacting to a returned value via an effect would land one commit later, and the re-snap would measure a layout without the strip.
[X3] R3 → R4 A focus move cancels any live hold before doing anything else. A hold armed by something the focus does not control (a resize, an active-segment
flip) keeps watching the content row, so the window slide the move causes would restart it and instant-scroll back to the abandoned group every frame.
[X4] R3 ↔ R4 While a glide is in flight a window-start move does not re-center — it sets windowChangedDuringScrollRef, and the glide’s own settle applies
the correction and then arms a hold. Centering instantly would land the strip on the target before the animation ran, turning the glide into a snap.
[X5] R5 → R2 The marker is the entire basis of R2’s fade / no-fade classification, and segmentationVersion is the entire basis of its edit / re-tokenization
classification. Anchor coordinates misclassify both, in both directions, which is why each needs an explicit out-of-band signal.
[X6] loader → R1 On a book load error the loader calls cancelFade(), aborting the in-flight fade without waiting for a settle that will never arrive.
